evidence: Cic. Cat. 2.1: in apertum latrōcinium (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cat. 2.10: nisi caedēs, nisi incendia, nisi rapīnās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In prose before Augustus, and in Tacitus and Suetonius, only in the plural (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: A robbery has just taken place.

phrases.latin: Arguentur dē vī et manū atque latrōciniō.
phrases.english: They will be charged with assault and battery as well as robbery.

sources: Lewis & Short: latrocinium · Lewis & Short: rapina
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 196, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
